papers.title: When Multimodal Fusion Fails: Contrastive Alignment as a Necessary Stabilizer for TCR–Peptide Binding Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multimodal learning is often assumed to improve predictive performance by combining complementary views, yet in biological applications auxiliary modalities are frequently imperfect, incomplete, or derived from upstream predictors and heuristics. We study this issue in TCR–peptide binding prediction, where sequence embeddings from pretrained protein language models are strong and transferable, but structure-derived residue graphs must be built from predicted folds and discretized contacts. These structural views can therefore be noisy, inconsistent across proteins, and sensitive to modeling choices, making them difficult to optimize jointly with sequence features. In this setting, naive sequence+graph fusion can destabilize training and degrade generalization, falling below a sequence-only baseline when supervision is scarce or contacts are noisy. This motivates a practical goal: use imperfect structural information when it helps, without sacrificing stability when it does not. Results We introduce TRACE, a lightweight framework that encodes each entity (TCR and peptide) with parallel sequence (frozen ESM-2) and residue-graph (GNN) towers, then applies CLIP-style intra-entity contrastive alignment before interaction modeling. The alignment encourages modality-consistent representations for the same biological entity, preventing noisy graph signals from dominating fusion. We evaluate under a leakage-controlled TCHard RN protocol with pair-disjoint splits, training-only model selection, and exclusion of negative-sampling metadata that otherwise trivially inflates AUROC. In this setting the task is near chance for all methods, and we do not claim state-of-the-art accuracy; our contribution is the failure-mode analysis, the alignment stabilizer, and the audited protocol itself. Among matched baselines TRACE attains the best mean AUROC (0.578±0.033 over five folds), and an ablation shows that intra-entity alignment acts as a stabilizer : it gives a small but consistent full-data gain (better on 4 of 5 folds), stays robust under substantial graph-edge corruption, and prevents collapse toward chance under limited supervision (+0.05 AUROC at 10–20% of labels), the regime where unconstrained fusion fails. How modalities are integrated, and how carefully they are evaluated, matters more than how many are used. Availability and implementation Code is available at https://github.com/MineSelf2016/TRACE and archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20635593 . Data are available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31991007

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：多模态学习通常被认为能够通过结合互补的信息来提升预测性能，但在生物学应用中，辅助模态数据往往存在缺陷、不完整，或是基于上游预测因子及启发式方法得出的。
llm_highlights_zh: 我们在TCR-肽段结合预测的研究中探讨了这一问题。其中，来自预训练蛋白质语言模型的序列嵌入模型具有很强的泛化能力且易于迁移应用；然而，基于结构信息构建的残基图谱则需要根据预测得到的蛋白质折叠结构及离散化的接触关系来生成。
因此，这些结构特征往往存在较大的不确定性，在不同蛋白质中可能表现出差异，并且会受到建模方法选择的显著影响，这使得它们难以与序列信息一起被有效地优化。
在这种环境下，单纯的序列数据与图结构信息的融合会破坏训练过程的稳定性，进而降低模型的泛化能力；当监督数据稀缺或接触信息存在噪声时，这种融合方法甚至会导致模型性能低于仅使用序列数据的基线水平。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
多模态学习通常被认为通过结合互补的信息来提升预测性能，但在生物学应用中，辅助模态数据往往存在缺陷、不完整，或是基于上游预测结果及启发式方法生成的。我们在TCR-肽段结合预测这一场景中研究了这一问题：虽然预训练的蛋白质语言模型能够生成有效的序列嵌入信息，但这些结构信息需要通过预测得到的蛋白质折叠结构和离散化的接触关系来构建，而这些数据本身可能存在噪声、在不同蛋白质间存在差异，并且对建模方法的选择非常敏感，因此很难与序列特征一起进行优化。在这种情况下，简单的序列与结构信息融合方式反而可能破坏训练过程的稳定性并降低模型的泛化能力；当监督数据不足或结构信息质量较差时，这种融合方法的性能甚至会低于仅使用序列信息的基线方法。因此，我们的研究目标是在结构信息不完善但仍有利用价值的情况下，合理地将其纳入预测模型中，同时确保模型的稳定性和准确性。  

**结果**  
我们提出了TRACE这一轻量级框架：该框架为每个生物实体（TCR或肽段）分别构建序列编码层（基于ESM-2模型）和残基图谱编码层（基于GNN模型），然后在交互作用建模之前应用CLIP风格的同实体对比对齐技术，以确保不同模态信息能够生成一致的表达结果，从而避免噪声较大的结构数据干扰融合过程。我们在严格控制数据泄露风险的实验环境中进行了评估，采用了成对独立的数据分割方式、仅基于训练数据的模型选择策略，并排除了那些会人为提高AUROC值的负样本元数据。在所有方法中，TRACE均取得了最佳的平均AUROC值（5次实验平均为0.578±0.033）；进一步的研究表明，这种同实体对比对齐机制起到了稳定模型的关键作用：它能够在数据质量较差的情况下仍为模型带来小幅但稳定的性能提升，在大量结构信息被破坏时依然保持有效，并且能在监督数据较少时防止模型性能下降（在仅10–20%的标签可用情况下，AUROC值仍能提高0.05）。  

**可获取性与实现方式**  
相关代码可访问https://github.com/MineSelf2016/TRACE，论文存档地址为https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20635593，数据集也可在相同链接下获取。

papers.title: MARD-Mol: A Hybrid Autoregressive-Diffusion Paradigm for Coarse-Grained Molecular Modeling
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Deep generative models have transformed drug molecule generation. However, molecules exhibit complex hierarchical structures, requiring models to simultaneously balance macroscopic topological coherence and microscopic chemical self-consistency. Although autoregressive and discrete diffusion paradigms are highly complementary, integrating their advantages within a unified architecture remains severely limited by traditional "atom-by-atom" fine-grained modeling. Results We propose MARD-Mol, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework based on motif-inspired units. By elevating the representation granularity from atoms to motif-inspired units and introducing a dual-stream hierarchical attention mechanism, it couples inter-unit autoregressive global scaffold planning with intra-unit discrete diffusion generation. To support goal-directed drug discovery, we reformulate property optimization into an iterative "diagnose-and-repair" process, enabling targeted optimization of defective motifs while preserving the global scaffold. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MARD-Mol achieves an 86.0% Quality score in de novo generation and exhibits superior performance in fragment-constrained and multi-objective optimization, establishing a new paradigm for high-quality drug design. Availability and Implementation The source code and datasets used in this study are available at GitHub: https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/MARD-Mol

To support goal-directed drug discovery, we reformulate property optimization into an iterative "diagnose-and-repair" process, enabling targeted optimization of defective motifs while preserving the global scaffold. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MARD-Mol achieves an 86.0% Quality score in de novo generation and exhibits superior performance in fragment-constrained and multi-objective optimization, establishing a new paradigm for high-quality drug design.

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
深度生成模型极大地推动了药物分子的设计过程。然而，药物分子具有复杂的层次结构，因此这些模型需要同时兼顾宏观的拓扑一致性与微观的化学稳定性。尽管自回归模型与离散扩散模型在原理上具有很强的互补性，但将它们的优势整合到统一的框架中仍受到传统“逐原子”建模方法的严重限制。

papers.primary_summary_raw: Deep generative models have transformed drug molecule generation. However, molecules exhibit complex hierarchical structures, requiring models to simultaneously balance macroscopic topological coherence and microscopic chemical self-consistency. Although autoregressive and discrete diffusion paradigms are highly complementary, integrating their advantages within a unified architecture remains severely limited by traditional "atom-by-atom" fine-grained modeling. Results We propose MARD-Mol, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework based on motif-inspired units. By elevating the representation granularity from atoms to motif-inspired units and introducing a dual-stream hierarchical attention mechanism, it couples inter-unit autoregressive global scaffold planning with intra-unit discrete diffusion generation. To support goal-directed drug discovery, we reformulate property optimization into an iterative "diagnose-and-repair" process, enabling targeted optimization of defective motifs while preserving the global scaffold. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MARD-Mol achieves an 86.0% Quality score in de novo generation and exhibits superior performance in fragment-constrained and multi-objective optimization, establishing a new paradigm for high-quality drug design.

papers.title: Drug Target Prediction from Perturbation Transcriptomics via a Biological Function-Guided Hypergraph Siamese Network
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Understanding how small molecules modulate cellular states remains a critical challenge in drug discovery. The advent of perturbation transcriptomics offers new avenues for elucidating drug-target interactions by capturing cellular transcriptional responses to perturbations. Results In this study, we propose BioHSNet, a biological function-guided hypergraph siamese network for inferring drug-target interactions from perturbation transcriptomics. BioHSNet utilizes hyperedge representations of functionally grouped gene expression to capture higher-order functional relationships, and integrates compound structural information into the model to bridge chemical structure and functional response. Experimental results demonstrate that BioHSNet outperforms other transcriptome-based methods on the Broad Institute’s L1000 datasets, particularly in cold start scenarios. The case study further demonstrates its practical utility for target prediction and drug screening. Availability and Implementation The source code is available at https://github.com/Zxinyizhang/BioHSNet

papers.title: ActivityDiff: A diffusion model with Positive and Negative Activity Guidance for De Novo Drug Design
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation De novo drug design requires not only promoting desired target activity, but also avoiding undesired target interactions that compromise selectivity and safety. However, existing generative models largely focus on optimizing positive activity, while overlooking negative activity information that could help suppress off-target effects during molecular design. Results We present ActivityDiff, a classifier-guided diffusion framework for activity-controlled molecular generation. Unlike conventional approaches that rely primarily on positive activity optimization, ActivityDiff explicitly incorporates both positive and negative guidance through separately trained drug-target classifiers. This design enables the model not only to promote desired target activities, but also to suppress harmful off-target interactions during generation. Experiments show that ActivityDiff effectively supports various drug design tasks, including single- and dual-target generation, fragment-constrained dual-target design, selective generation for improved target specificity, and reduction of off-target effects. These results demonstrate that classifier-guided diffusion with explicit negative guidance provides an effective strategy for jointly optimizing efficacy and safety in molecular design. Availability The source code can be obtained from https://github.com/e-yi/ActivityDiff

从头药物设计不仅需要增强目标分子的活性，还需避免那些会降低选择性及安全性的非目标相互作用。然而现有的生成模型大多侧重于优化分子的正面活性，而忽视了那些有助于抑制脱靶效应的负面信息。

MOTIVATION: De novo drug design requires not only promoting desired target activity, but also avoiding undesired target interactions that compromise selectivity and safety. all_papers.title: When Multimodal Fusion Fails: Contrastive Alignment as a Necessary Stabilizer for TCR–Peptide Binding Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multimodal learning is often assumed to improve predictive performance by combining complementary views, yet in biological applications auxiliary modalities are frequently imperfect, incomplete, or derived from upstream predictors and heuristics. We study this issue in TCR–peptide binding prediction, where sequence embeddings from pretrained protein language models are strong and transferable, but structure-derived residue graphs must be built from predicted folds and discretized contacts. These structural views can therefore be noisy, inconsistent across proteins, and sensitive to modeling choices, making them difficult to optimize jointly with sequence features. In this setting, naive sequence+graph fusion can destabilize training and degrade generalization, falling below a sequence-only baseline when supervision is scarce or contacts are noisy. This motivates a practical goal: use imperfect structural information when it helps, without sacrificing stability when it does not. Results We introduce TRACE, a lightweight framework that encodes each entity (TCR and peptide) with parallel sequence (frozen ESM-2) and residue-graph (GNN) towers, then applies CLIP-style intra-entity contrastive alignment before interaction modeling. The alignment encourages modality-consistent representations for the same biological entity, preventing noisy graph signals from dominating fusion. We evaluate under a leakage-controlled TCHard RN protocol with pair-disjoint splits, training-only model selection, and exclusion of negative-sampling metadata that otherwise trivially inflates AUROC. In this setting the task is near chance for all methods, and we do not claim state-of-the-art accuracy; our contribution is the failure-mode analysis, the alignment stabilizer, and the audited protocol itself. Among matched baselines TRACE attains the best mean AUROC (0.578±0.033 over five folds), and an ablation shows that intra-entity alignment acts as a stabilizer : it gives a small but consistent full-data gain (better on 4 of 5 folds), stays robust under substantial graph-edge corruption, and prevents collapse toward chance under limited supervision (+0.05 AUROC at 10–20% of labels), the regime where unconstrained fusion fails. How modalities are integrated, and how carefully they are evaluated, matters more than how many are used. Availability and implementation Code is available at https://github.com/MineSelf2016/TRACE and archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20635593 . Data are available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31991007

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
多模态学习通常被认为通过结合互补的信息来提升预测性能，但在生物学应用中，辅助模态数据往往存在缺陷、不完整，或是基于上游预测结果及启发式方法生成的。我们在TCR-肽段结合预测这一场景中研究了这一问题：虽然预训练的蛋白质语言模型能够生成有效的序列嵌入信息，但这些结构信息需要通过预测得到的蛋白质折叠结构和离散化的接触关系来构建，而这些数据本身可能存在噪声、在不同蛋白质间存在差异，并且对建模方法的选择非常敏感，因此很难与序列特征一起进行优化。在这种情况下，简单的序列与结构信息融合方式反而可能破坏训练过程的稳定性并降低模型的泛化能力；当监督数据不足或结构信息质量较差时，这种融合方法的性能甚至会低于仅使用序列信息的基线方法。因此，我们的研究目标是在结构信息不完善但仍有利用价值的情况下，合理地将其纳入预测模型中，同时确保模型的稳定性和准确性。  

**结果**  
我们提出了TRACE这一轻量级框架：该框架为每个生物实体（TCR或肽段）分别构建序列编码层（基于ESM-2模型）和残基图谱编码层（基于GNN模型），然后在交互作用建模之前应用CLIP风格的同实体对比对齐技术，以确保不同模态信息能够生成一致的表达结果，从而避免噪声较大的结构数据干扰融合过程。我们在严格控制数据泄露风险的实验环境中进行了评估，采用了成对独立的数据分割方式、仅基于训练数据的模型选择策略，并排除了那些会人为提高AUROC值的负样本元数据。在所有方法中，TRACE均取得了最佳的平均AUROC值（5次实验平均为0.578±0.033）；进一步的研究表明，这种同实体对比对齐机制起到了稳定模型的关键作用：它能够在数据质量较差的情况下仍为模型带来小幅但稳定的性能提升，在大量结构信息被破坏时依然保持有效，并且能在监督数据较少时防止模型性能下降（在仅10–20%的标签可用情况下，AUROC值仍能提高0.05）。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Multimodal learning is often assumed to improve predictive performance by combining complementary views, yet in biological applications auxiliary modalities are frequently imperfect, incomplete, or derived from upstream predictors and heuristics. We study this issue in TCR–peptide binding prediction, where sequence embeddings from pretrained protein language models are strong and transferable, but structure-derived residue graphs must be built from predicted folds and discretized contacts. These structural views can therefore be noisy, inconsistent across proteins, and sensitive to modeling choices, making them difficult to optimize jointly with sequence features. In this setting, naive sequence+graph fusion can destabilize training and degrade generalization, falling below a sequence-only baseline when supervision is scarce or contacts are noisy. This motivates a practical goal: use imperfect structural information when it helps, without sacrificing stability when it does not. Results We introduce TRACE, a lightweight framework that encodes each entity (TCR and peptide) with parallel sequence (frozen ESM-2) and residue-graph (GNN) towers, then applies CLIP-style intra-entity contrastive alignment before interaction modeling. The alignment encourages modality-consistent representations for the same biological entity, preventing noisy graph signals from dominating fusion. We evaluate under a leakage-controlled TCHard RN protocol with pair-disjoint splits, training-only model selection, and exclusion of negative-sampling metadata that otherwise trivially inflates AUROC. In this setting the task is near chance for all methods, and we do not claim state-of-the-art accuracy; our contribution is the failure-mode analysis, the alignment stabilizer, and the audited protocol itself. Among matched baselines TRACE attains the best mean AUROC (0.578±0.033 over five folds), and an ablation shows that intra-entity alignment acts as a stabilizer : it gives a small but consistent full-data gain (better on 4 of 5 folds), stays robust under substantial graph-edge corruption, and prevents collapse toward chance under limited supervision (+0.05 AUROC at 10–20% of labels), the regime where unconstrained fusion fails. How modalities are integrated, and how carefully they are evaluated, matters more than how many are used.

all_papers.title: MARD-Mol: A Hybrid Autoregressive-Diffusion Paradigm for Coarse-Grained Molecular Modeling
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Deep generative models have transformed drug molecule generation. However, molecules exhibit complex hierarchical structures, requiring models to simultaneously balance macroscopic topological coherence and microscopic chemical self-consistency. Although autoregressive and discrete diffusion paradigms are highly complementary, integrating their advantages within a unified architecture remains severely limited by traditional "atom-by-atom" fine-grained modeling. Results We propose MARD-Mol, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework based on motif-inspired units. By elevating the representation granularity from atoms to motif-inspired units and introducing a dual-stream hierarchical attention mechanism, it couples inter-unit autoregressive global scaffold planning with intra-unit discrete diffusion generation. To support goal-directed drug discovery, we reformulate property optimization into an iterative "diagnose-and-repair" process, enabling targeted optimization of defective motifs while preserving the global scaffold. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MARD-Mol achieves an 86.0% Quality score in de novo generation and exhibits superior performance in fragment-constrained and multi-objective optimization, establishing a new paradigm for high-quality drug design. Availability and Implementation The source code and datasets used in this study are available at GitHub: https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/MARD-Mol

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
深度生成模型极大地推动了药物分子的设计过程。然而，药物分子具有复杂的层次结构，因此这些模型需要同时兼顾宏观的拓扑一致性与微观的化学稳定性。尽管自回归模型与离散扩散模型在原理上具有很强的互补性，但将它们的优势整合到统一的框架中仍受到传统“逐原子”建模方法的严重限制。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了MARD-Mol这一基于结构基序的混合式自回归-扩散框架。通过将表征层次从原子提升到结构基序，并引入双流层次注意力机制，该模型成功地将单元间的自回归全局结构规划与单元内的离散扩散生成过程相结合。为支持目标导向的药物发现，我们还将性质优化过程重构为迭代式的“诊断与修复”流程，从而能够有针对性地修改存在缺陷的结构基序，同时保持分子的整体结构稳定性。大量实验结果表明，MARD-Mol在新药分子的从头设计中取得了86.0%的优质度评分，在片段约束条件及多目标优化任务中也表现出显著的优势，为高质量药物设计开辟了新的途径。

all_papers.title: Drug Target Prediction from Perturbation Transcriptomics via a Biological Function-Guided Hypergraph Siamese Network
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Understanding how small molecules modulate cellular states remains a critical challenge in drug discovery. The advent of perturbation transcriptomics offers new avenues for elucidating drug-target interactions by capturing cellular transcriptional responses to perturbations. Results In this study, we propose BioHSNet, a biological function-guided hypergraph siamese network for inferring drug-target interactions from perturbation transcriptomics. BioHSNet utilizes hyperedge representations of functionally grouped gene expression to capture higher-order functional relationships, and integrates compound structural information into the model to bridge chemical structure and functional response. Experimental results demonstrate that BioHSNet outperforms other transcriptome-based methods on the Broad Institute’s L1000 datasets, particularly in cold start scenarios. The case study further demonstrates its practical utility for target prediction and drug screening. Availability and Implementation The source code is available at https://github.com/Zxinyizhang/BioHSNet

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Understanding how small molecules modulate cellular states remains a critical challenge in drug discovery. The advent of perturbation transcriptomics offers new avenues for elucidating drug-target interactions by capturing cellular transcriptional responses to perturbations. Results In this study, we propose BioHSNet, a biological function-guided hypergraph siamese network for inferring drug-target interactions from perturbation transcriptomics. BioHSNet utilizes hyperedge representations of functionally grouped gene expression to capture higher-order functional relationships, and integrates compound structural information into the model to bridge chemical structure and functional response. Experimental results demonstrate that BioHSNet outperforms other transcriptome-based methods on the Broad Institute’s L1000 datasets, particularly in cold start scenarios. The case study further demonstrates its practical utility for target prediction and drug screening.

all_papers.title: ActivityDiff: A diffusion model with Positive and Negative Activity Guidance for De Novo Drug Design
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation De novo drug design requires not only promoting desired target activity, but also avoiding undesired target interactions that compromise selectivity and safety. However, existing generative models largely focus on optimizing positive activity, while overlooking negative activity information that could help suppress off-target effects during molecular design. Results We present ActivityDiff, a classifier-guided diffusion framework for activity-controlled molecular generation. Unlike conventional approaches that rely primarily on positive activity optimization, ActivityDiff explicitly incorporates both positive and negative guidance through separately trained drug-target classifiers. This design enables the model not only to promote desired target activities, but also to suppress harmful off-target interactions during generation. Experiments show that ActivityDiff effectively supports various drug design tasks, including single- and dual-target generation, fragment-constrained dual-target design, selective generation for improved target specificity, and reduction of off-target effects. These results demonstrate that classifier-guided diffusion with explicit negative guidance provides an effective strategy for jointly optimizing efficacy and safety in molecular design. Availability The source code can be obtained from https://github.com/e-yi/ActivityDiff

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
从头药物设计不仅需要增强目标分子的活性，还需避免那些会降低选择性及安全性的非目标相互作用。然而现有的生成模型大多侧重于优化分子的正面活性，而忽视了那些有助于抑制脱靶效应的负面信息。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了ActivityDiff——一种基于分类器引导的扩散框架，用于实现活性可控的分子设计。与传统主要依赖正面活性优化的方法不同，ActivityDiff通过分别训练的药物-靶标分类器，同时整合了正面与负面的指导信息。这种设计使模型既能有效增强目标分子的活性，又能在生成过程中抑制有害的脱靶效应。实验结果表明，ActivityDiff能够高效支持多种药物设计任务，包括单靶点/双靶点分子的设计、受片段结构限制的双靶点优化、旨在提升靶标选择性的分子筛选，以及减少脱靶效应的处理。这些结果充分证明了：基于分类器引导且包含负面指导信息的扩散模型，为分子设计中同时优化药效与安全性提供了有效策略。  

**代码获取方式**  
源代码可访问以下链接获取：  
https://github.com/e-yi/ActivityDiff
